NVDA.supply_chain_summary: NVIDIA sits at the apex of the AI compute supply chain, designing cutting-edge GPU and networking silicon that is exclusively manufactured by TSMC using advanced nodes, with critical dependencies on HBM memory from SK Hynix/Samsung and EUV equipment from ASML. On the demand side, NVIDIA's revenue is heavily concentrated among a small number of hyperscale cloud providers (Microsoft, Amazon, Google, Meta) racing to build AI infrastructure, giving these downstream customers significant collective leverage while simultaneously creating powerful, sticky demand dynamics.

AAPL.supply_chain_summary: Apple sits at the apex of a highly sophisticated consumer electronics supply chain, acting as a powerful systems integrator that designs its own silicon but relies on a concentrated network of Asian foundries, display makers, and component suppliers to manufacture its products. On the downstream side, Apple distributes primarily through carriers, its own retail stores, and online channels, while also monetizing its massive installed base of ~2 billion active devices through high-margin services including the App Store, licensing deals, and subscriptions.

MU.supply_chain_summary: Micron Technology sits at the heart of the global memory supply chain, heavily dependent on a concentrated set of semiconductor equipment makers (ASML, AMAT, LRCX) for its capital-intensive DRAM and NAND manufacturing. On the demand side, Micron's revenue is increasingly driven by AI infrastructure buildout — particularly HBM sales to NVIDIA — alongside sustained consumption from hyperscalers (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud) and mobile OEMs like Apple.

ARM.supply_chain_summary: Arm Holdings sits at a uniquely central position in the global semiconductor ecosystem as an IP licensor rather than a manufacturer, collecting royalties and license fees from virtually every major chip designer who builds on its CPU, GPU, and NPU architectures. Its upstream dependencies are primarily EDA software vendors and process validation partnerships with foundries, while its downstream reach spans the entire semiconductor industry — from mobile and PC OEMs to hyperscale cloud providers and automotive chipmakers — making it one of the most broadly embedded technology IP platforms in existence.

MRVL.supply_chain_summary: Marvell Technology sits at the intersection of advanced semiconductor design and cloud infrastructure, acting as a fabless chip designer that relies heavily on TSMC for leading-edge fabrication and ARM/EDA vendors for IP and design tools. Its downstream is increasingly dominated by hyperscale cloud providers (Amazon, Google, Meta, Microsoft) who consume custom AI ASICs and high-speed networking silicon, making Marvell a critical enabler of AI data center buildouts.
